source: Written from memory by a Claude session on October 30, 2026, then checked on November 2, 2026: every Senate row against the senate.gov roster XML (last updated October 8, 2026), every governor row against the NGA roster and Wikipedia, and winners against the local results/ files where present. Recheck for vacancies or appointments after October 8 before air.
notes: Holdovers are the seats NOT on the 2026 ballot. Seats up are in `up`, copied from data/reference/races_2026_seed.csv so the wall reads one file (scripts/serve.py --public allows only this reference file).
Independents are listed with their own party and counted on the board by `caucus`.
The wall sums these rows itself and shows a warning if they disagree with `totals` or with the expected 65 Senate / 14 governor holdovers.

held_2024.note: Seats won in November 2024. Vacancies and special elections since are not reflected; the board's House 'held' is the 2024 winner of the same-numbered district.

redrawn_for_2026.note: Mid-decade maps change what 'the same-numbered district' means. List the states the board should flag; leave empty if unsure.
redrawn_for_2026.source: Checked November 1, 2026 against Census TIGER/Line 2026 cd120 (the 120th Congress) vs cb_2024 cd119: these nine states have districts that moved (worst same-number overlap 0.00-0.48); every other state overlaps 0.99+. Missouri is the exception: Census cd120 has its 2025 map (MO-05 overlap 0.02), but the user confirmed November 1 that Missouri votes on its 2022 map, so MO is not on this list and draws from geo/congress.topojson. The map draws these nine from geo/congress-2026.topojson.

first_round_runoff.note: States whose November House races are open all-party first rounds, with a runoff when nobody passes 50%. A leader there is a round-one leader, not the presumptive winner.
first_round_runoff.source: states-south-east, November 1, 2026: Louisiana's 2026 House races carry IsClosedParty:0, CanHaveRunoff:1 in the Secretary of State's results data, with 4-10 candidates each.
